127.0.s.en: (1) The blessing of those who love Him

127.0.0.en: Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it. Except the LORD keep the city, the watchman wakes but in vain.

127.0.1.en: 1- In this verse Solomon shows that God is the foundation of success in everything that is for building, and also in guarding our life and keeping it, so that those returning from captivity are not disturbed when the enemies oppose them; for as long as God is with them they will succeed in building the temple and Jerusalem and renewing its walls and gates.

127.0.2.en: 2- This verse shows the work of the supporting grace in the spiritual striving, for man's abilities are limited and few before the power of Satan. But God's supporting grace makes man stronger than Satan, and this calls the striving man to faith in God and reliance on Him, with caution against negligence, because it angers God, and also because relying on human strength alone must lead to failure.

127.0.3.en: 3- Although Satan opposed Christ and made the Jews crucify Him, and still opposes the Church of God in the New Testament to this day, he is helpless before the grace of God that has established the Church until today, and she will remain established for ever through the power of the faith of God's children, their reliance on Him, and their continual self-giving for the sake of His love.

127.1.0.en: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of toils. But

127.1.2.en: 1- When a person is occupied with material goods, and rises early for them to work a long time, and does not sit down to rest, and finds no opportunity for prayer or reading in the word of God, his heart is filled with worry, and he eats his food with troubles and psychological distress. On the contrary, whoever relies on God and does his duty in life is happy, and God gives him peace in his steps and during his sleep, so he lives in constant joy.

127.1.3.en: 2- God gave His beloved sleep when Christ slept on the Cross, that is, died for our redemption, and then rose on the third day.

127.1.4.en: Relying on God gives peace, and even makes a person active and able to accomplish greater works. Therefore do not weary yourself with worry and too much thinking, but do your duty and leave God to complete every weakness and lack in you.

127.2.s.en: (2) Children are a blessing from the Lord

127.2.0.en: (Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD, and the fruit of the womb is a reward.

127.2.1.en: 1- From ancient times, and even now in many parts of the world, a multitude of children is considered a blessing from God, and the Law of Moses declares this (Deut 28:4, 11).

127.2.2.en: 2- If a multitude of children is a blessing from the Lord, then all the more the spiritual children born of the font of Baptism in the Church of the New Testament are a blessing from the Lord, and new members in His body, which is the Church, that He may be glorified in them when they live with Him and keep His commandments. For Christ paid His blood as the price for acquiring His children who are born of the font of Baptism; they are His reward, because He bought them with His blood.

127.3.0.en: (As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man, so are children of the youth.

127.3.2.en: 1- When a young woman gives birth, her children are physically strong; so the children of youth are strong, but their true strength is that they are in the hand of a mighty man, who is God. An arrow, however strong and sharp, reaches its target when it is placed in the hand of a mighty man. So also the spiritual children of God, who declared His name in the Old and New Testaments, that is, the prophets and Apostles and all the priests and servants.

127.3.3.en: 2- Youth signifies strength, for Christ accomplished His redemption on the Cross with power, and freed Adam and his children and brought them up to Paradise, and gave power to everyone who believes in Him, so that he overcomes Satan.

127.4.0.en: (Happy is the man that has his quiver full of them; they shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate.

127.4.1.en: Happy: how blessed and joyful he is. Quiver: the quiver is the pouch, that is, a leather bag in which arrows are placed.

127.4.2.en: 1- He who has strong sons, when the enemies come, does not let them into the city, but they stand at its gate, and the sons confront the messengers sent by the enemies with strength, and reject their threats or their deceit.

127.4.3.en: 2- The strong sons who are the arrows signify spiritually the words of God with which a person confronts the wars of Satan, as Christ did in the temptation on the mountain; and the arrows also, that is, the strong sons, are the spiritual weapons in general, such as faith and truth and righteousness) ... Eph 6:13-17), and likewise the spiritual virtues; all of these can repel the attacks of the devil and overcome him.

127.4.4.en: May you fill your mind with spiritual thoughts, and your heart with feelings toward God, so that you may fight and overcome Satan; for the power of God gives you victory always, however great the devil's cunning or power.

127.4.5.en: The blessings of the godly. A song of ascents. “Blessed is every one that fears the LORD; that walks in His ways) “... v. 1. Introduction:

127.4.6.en: 1- Its writer: unknown; it is one of the orphan psalms whose writer is not known.

127.4.7.en: 2- This psalm is distinguished by its speaking of the spiritual family in the home, of the wife and the children and the grandchildren.

127.4.8.en: 3- This psalm encourages the one who prays it to fear the Lord, that he may enjoy blessings in his life and in his home.

127.4.9.en: 4- This psalm is prayed on the ninth step on the way of the ascent to the temple of the Lord.

127.4.10.en: 5- This psalm encourages those who returned from captivity in small numbers, that as long as they fear God, and have returned to build His house and worship Him, He will bless them and multiply their offspring, and they will live in God's good things.

127.4.11.en: 6- This psalm signifies Christ, for He is the man who fears the LORD, and his wife is the Church, and his children are the believers in Him throughout the generations; in this respect it is considered one of the Messianic psalms.

127.4.12.en: 7- The Church reads part of this psalm in the rite of the Crowning prayer.

127.4.13.en: 8- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Vespers, because it promises the man who fears the LORD, who has lived in the fear of God all day long, many blessings that encourage him to continue his life in the fear of the Lord for the rest of his days.

128.0.0.en: Blessed is every one that fears the LORD; that walks in His ways.

128.0.1.en: 1- The psalm shows the happiness of him who fears the LORD, for he receives spiritual and material good things, in addition to the eternal good things; because he fears God, he keeps His commandments, and walks in the ways of the Lord, which are the commandments and the means of grace.

128.0.2.en: 2- This verse is a prophecy about the salvation of the Gentiles, and everyone who fears the LORD, so believes in Him and lives with Him and joins the people of God and walks in His ways; for reaching God has many forms in life, such as marriage, or monasticism, or serving virginity.

128.0.3.en: 3- This verse is also a prophecy about Christ, who lived in godliness all His days on the earth, and walked in the ways of the Lord and did not commit a single sin, and fulfilled all righteousness.

128.1.0.en: For you shall eat the labour of your hands; happy shall you be, and it shall be well with you.

128.1.1.en: 1- This verse shows the importance of work and spiritual striving; whoever toils, God gives him blessings and good things. Work is necessary, since Adam was working in the garden to till the ground and to name the animals with their names. And Paul tells us of the importance of work, saying “If any would not work, neither should he eat) “(2 Thess 3:10)

128.1.2.en: 2- The good things received by him who works or strives spiritually, he receives their recompense partly on the earth, and then a great, inexpressible reward in heaven. All this is for him who toils and so receives; but beware lest anyone wrong another and take his toil, that is, take the reward of another's toil.

128.2.0.en: Your wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of your house; your children like olive plants round about your table.

128.3.0.en: (Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that fears the LORD.

128.3.1.en: 1- All the previous good things and blessings that the psalm mentioned come upon the man who fears the LORD, and God loves those who fear Him, because they believe in His name and walk by His commandments, so He blesses them with countless spiritual and material blessings. The world cannot take away these blessings, because they are from God, unlike the temporary, passing good things of the world. All these blessings are accompanied by peace in the heart of him who fears God, and great joy; all this is a prelude to the blessings that surpass the mind, which he receives in heaven.

128.4.0.en: (The LORD shall bless you out of Zion, and you shall see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life.

128.4.1.en: 1- The blessings that come upon him who fears the LORD come to him from Jerusalem, that is, from the temple of the Lord; so they are blessings from God, and not from the passing world.

128.4.2.en: 2- The one who fears the LORD sees the good of Jerusalem, not only the material good things, such as rebuilding the temple after the return from captivity, or its renewal in the days of King Herod, or material good things for the holy city of God, but rather the spiritual good things, which appear in the fullness of time through Christ the Redeemer, who offers in Jerusalem salvation to the whole world. Blessings overflow from the Church of the New Testament in the whole world, while the fullness of blessings and good is in the heavenly Jerusalem.

128.4.3.en: Remember God's previous works with you, that your faith may be established and you may rely on Him, and the lusts of the world may not be able to lure you, so that you are with Him with all your heart.

128.5.0.en: (Yea, you shall see your children's children. Peace be upon Israel.

128.5.1.en: 1- He gives a new blessing to him who fears the LORD, which is length of days of life on the earth, so that he sees his grandchildren; for he who fears the LORD enjoys peace and joy, and so lives in quietness a long life. As in ancient times a multitude of children was a blessing from God.

128.5.2.en: 2- The children's children are the spiritual children whom the priests and servants in the New Testament, and all who spoke in the name of the Lord in the Old Testament, such as the prophets, enjoy seeing, that is, those who are taught at the hands of these and the hands of their children, as appears in the life of the monastic fathers and the bishops and the celibates consecrated to the service of God in the world.

128.5.3.en: 3- The psalm ends by invoking peace upon all the people of God, filled with the godly who live in God's blessings, the most important of which is inner peace.

128.5.4.en: Good things await you as much as you fear God; so remember God's justice, and walk in repentance at all times, and keep the commandments of the Lord, and enjoy confession and Communion, and you will live in peace all your days.

128.5.5.en: The Lord delivers the afflicted. A song of ascents. “Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Israel now say) “.. v. 1. Introduction:

128.5.6.en: 1- Its writer: unknown; it is one of the orphan psalms whose writer is not known.

128.5.7.en: 2- There is a great similarity between this psalm and (Ps 124), which is also one of the psalms of ascents, “If it had not been the LORD”.... so that some believe that their writer is one, the prophet David. We see in both psalms that the first and second verses are repeated, and each presents the suffering of God's children, and then shows God's love that keeps them and delivers them.

128.5.8.en: 3- Although those who fear the LORD receive many blessings, as appears in the previous psalm, Satan also fights them much, and God delivers them and takes vengeance on the wicked, as appears in this psalm.

128.5.9.en: 4- This psalm suits everyone who suffers afflictions, for it strengthens him and gives him hope in God's protection and His rescue of him.

128.5.10.en: 5- This psalm is prayed on the tenth step on the way of the ascent to the temple.

128.5.11.en: 6- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Agpeya in the prayer of Vespers, to encourage the spiritual striver who has borne many toils all day long that God is with him, and will deliver him from the hands of his enemies, and even take vengeance on them.

129.0.0.en: “Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth,” let Israel now say, “many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, yet they have not prevailed against me.

129.0.1.en: 1- God's children are exposed to afflictions from the wicked from their youth, that is, from their childhood until the end of their life, but what encourages them to endure is that their enemies are not able to prevail against them, because God is with them.

129.0.2.en: 2- All the righteous bore afflictions even when the number of people in the world was very small: Cain afflicted Abel, and Noah was mocked by the whole world when he built the ark, and he may have endured much even from the hired workmen who made the ark; and the people of Israel bore at the beginning of its life severe afflictions in Egypt, then in the wilderness of Sinai and the war of Amalek, and afterward in wars with the inhabitants of Canaan, and was exposed to the humiliation of the Assyrian and Babylonian captivity, yet they enjoyed God's dwelling among them and His blessings. And if David is the writer, he bore many afflictions from Saul, then Absalom, but God was with him and delivered him from their hands and made him king over his people and gave him the joy of His fellowship.

129.1.0.en: (The plowers plowed upon my back; they made long their furrows.”

129.1.1.en: Their furrows: plural of furrow, which is the line dug in the ground that the plow makes as it passes over the ground.

129.1.2.en: 1- The writer of the psalm makes clear the extent of the suffering he bore from the wicked, who struck him and scourged him and left cruel marks on his back, and his blood flowed. And as the plow passes through the ground and splits it, making deep lines in it, so also the wicked plowed upon his back, that is, they scourged him, and split his back with deep lines (furrows), that is, he bore and suffered much for the sake of God. For the purity of the righteous rebukes the wicked, so they mistreat them violently.

129.1.3.en: 2- Although the plow splits the ground, afterward the seeds are placed in these deep lines and the plants grow and give fruit; so also bearing sufferings gives the soul strength, and a blessing from God, so it grows in righteousness and virtue, and bears the fruits of the Holy Spirit.

129.1.4.en: 3- Christ bore the scourging on His back and the Crucifixion and gave us salvation. So also the priests and servants bear many troubles from the flock, and carry their burdens, so that they may know God with a true knowledge, and their harsh natures may change.

129.1.5.en: Bear with those around you for the sake of Christ who bore with you, and know that this endurance proves your life, so you become worthy of many blessings on the earth and in heaven.

129.2.0.en: (The LORD is righteous; He has cut asunder the cords of the wicked.

129.2.1.en: The cords of the wicked: the cords are the ropes by which the yoke is fastened, which is a piece of wood fixed on the necks of the two animals and tied at the neck, so that the yoke rests upon them.

129.2.2.en: 1- God intervenes when He sees the cruelty of the wicked toward His children, and He likens the burdens they place on His children to the yoke that is tied on the necks of animals; if these cords are cut they are freed from the cruelty of the wicked, and go far away from them. So God lifts the trial and gives rest to His children, and even blesses them with many comforts. This gives hope to the suffering that the trial is temporary, and God will surely end it.

129.3.0.en: (Let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Zion. Let them be as the grass upon the housetops, which withers before it grows up, wherewith the mower fills not his hand, nor he that binds sheaves his bosom.

129.3.1.en: Zion: the most important of the five hills on which the city of Jerusalem was built, and by Zion he means Jerusalem, in which the believers in the Lord live.

129.3.2.en: The binder: the one who gathers plants into sheaves.

129.3.3.en: 1- God declares that the wicked who hate His children will be overtaken by shame, and even be turned back, and leave off harming His children. He also likens their evils against His children to the grass of the housetops, that is, the small plants that grow on the roofs of village houses in a thin layer of soil, so the roots of these grasses have no depth, and they dry up from the heat of the sun and die quickly. Before these grasses grow, and the farmer gathers them and puts them in sheaves to feed his cattle, they dry up and are thrown far away to be burned, because there is no use in them. So also the evils of the wicked are superficial, with a strong appearance, but they end quickly.

129.3.4.en: 2- All the persecutions directed against the Church throughout the ages are brought to nothing, and the demons are put to shame and turn back, because all their evils are superficial, since God dwells in His children, so they are not disturbed by the persecutions, and they end quickly, and even His children grow in their love for God.

129.4.0.en: (Neither do they which go by say, “The blessing of the LORD be upon you; we bless you in the name of the LORD.”

129.4.1.en: 1- It becomes clear before all people who pass by the wicked, whom he previously likened to the grass of the housetops, that the wicked have no power, and receive no blessing from God, for they dry up and are burned, as a pointer to their destiny, which is eternal torment in the blazing fire.

129.4.2.en: 2- On the other side, God's children receive a blessing in the name of the Lord, because of their walking in righteousness and their bearing persecution from the wicked for the sake of the Lord.

129.4.3.en: The success of the wicked seems great but it is temporary and passing, so do not heed it, and stand firm in your faith in God and His commandments, and you will live in peace on the earth, and then in inexpressible happiness in heaven.

129.4.4.en: H Forgiveness and redemption. A song of ascents. “Out of the depths have I cried unto You, O LORD) “... v. 1. Introduction:

129.4.5.en: 1- Its writer: unknown; it is one of the orphan psalms whose writer's name is not mentioned in the title; but there is an inclination that he is the prophet David.

129.4.6.en: 2- When was it written? In the days of David, because Solomon quoted from it in his prayer (v. 2; 2 Chr 6:40-42).

129.4.7.en: 3- Perhaps Nehemiah quoted from this psalm in his book and in his prayer (v. 2; Neh 1:6, 11)

129.4.8.en: 4- This psalm is also similar to the Epistles of St. Paul the Apostle, especially (Rom 7, 8). This confirms the unity of the Holy Bible, for the Holy Spirit is the inspirer of all the books of the Old and New Testaments.

129.4.9.en: 5- This psalm suits the penitent person who asks forgiveness from God, for it develops his hope and his reliance on Him.

129.4.10.en: 6- This psalm suits those returning from captivity, for it gives them hope in the new life with God.

129.4.11.en: 7- This psalm is one of the well-known penitential psalms mentioned before, which are seven psalms: (Ps 6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143)

129.4.12.en: 8- This psalm shows God's concern for the depths of man, that is, his heart and his feelings, more than his outward appearance.

129.4.13.en: 9- This psalm is one of the Messianic psalms, because it speaks to us of Christ the Redeemer (vv. 6-8).

129.4.14.en: 10- This psalm used to be prayed on the eleventh step on the way of the ascent to the temple of the Lord.

129.4.15.en: 11- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Compline, for we offer repentance before God and ask His forgiveness for all our sins, in preparation for a new day, not only on the earth, but for the day that has no end, that is, eternity.
